events.description:
Philly Hardware
Join us for the 14th Philadelphia Hardware Meetup! Come join us to hear from our guest speakers as well as share whatâs on your desk. We always have time for an open mic.

***[Please click here to RSVP on Luma!](https://luma.com/qxtaofeu)***

âââThis time, we're back at **Delve's** office on Arch Street.

â*Hardware Meetups happen across 30+ cities monthly and help bring together different professionals to connect and meet each other.*

â**We will have a great set of featured speakers for the evening!:**

* â[Dan Lykens](https://www.linkedin.com/in/danlykens/?utm_source=luma), Electromechanical Engineer at [Production Systems Automation](https://www.psasystems.com/?utm_source=luma). Dan is a multidisciplinary engineer and entrepreneur with over a decade of experience in electromechanical systems, PCB design, and product development. At PSA, he leads defense-focused R&D projects, specializing in rugged electronics. Dan combines deep technical proficiency in PCB design, CAD modeling, and advanced prototyping techniques.
* â[David Levine](https://www.linkedin.com/in/david-j-levine/), Senior Solutions Engineer, [Viam](https://viam.com). Viam is a software platform for building, deploying, and managing robotics applications. Viam brings software engineering practices to robotics: version control, remote monitoring and diagnostics, staged rollouts, and a registry of modules and models you can build on. At Viam, David is one of the leaders of robotic solution design -- including hardware, electronics, safety systems, and supporting software -- for automation customers across various industries. Prior to joining Viam, David received his Ph.D. in Mechanical Engineering from UPenn in 2023 and B.S. in Mechanical Engineering from Cornell in 2017, and previously founded a robotics startup in the Philadelphia ecosystem, which was later supported by the Cornell Tech Runway Postdoctoral Fellowship.
* [Daniel Marcq](https://www.linkedin.com/in/daniel-marcq-jr/), Client Partner and Senior Director of Electrical & Software Engineering at [Delve](http://www.delve.com/). Dan leads the development of complex hardware and connected systems from early strategy through commercialization. Since joining Delve in 2019, he has led multidisciplinary programs spanning electrical engineering, embedded systems, robotics, sensing, controls, and software for medical devices and other advanced products.

â**Thank you to our partners!:**

âWeâre excited to welcome **[Efinix](https://www.efinixinc.com/index.html?utm_source=luma)** as a sponsor of our next Philadelphia Hardware Meetup!
Efinix manufactures the worldâs most efficient FPGAs. Delivering low power, high performance and small physical size, Efinix FPGAs offer fast time to market in a cost-effective footprint. Efinix offers three families of FPGAs from the entry level Trion family that prioritizes I/O and connectivity to the Titanium family that offer high speed transceivers and high compute capability for industrial, edge and highly accelerated AI applications. The portfolio spans 4,000 logic elements up 375,000 logic elements and includes SiP offering with Flash and system memory in the same FPGA package. These highly integrated solutions reduce design complexity, increase available I/O and further speed time to market. The Efinix Efinity tool suite is freely available and delivers an intuitive RTL to bit-stream capability while supporting a rich IP library and software compilers for the suite of Sapphire RISC-V processors available as both hard IP and soft macros across the Efinix portfolio.
Efinix FPGAs have been widely adopted in a broad array of markets from industrial automation , communications, medical, automotive and test and measurement. To find out more about Efinix products and markets, visit [www.efinixinc.com](http://www.efinixinc.com/ "http://www.efinixinc.com").
Thank you to Efinix for supporting the Philadelphia hardware community and helping bring local engineers, founders, and product developers together.
